title: Presumed first episode of nonconvulsive status epilepticus as the cause of postoperative disorder of consciousness following the completion of general anesthesia: A case report
case_prompt: An man in his 80s (height 148 cm, weight 50 kg) with hypertension and a history of asymptomatic cerebral infarction (on aspirin) underwent surgical excision of extramammary Paget's disease under general anesthesia. Preoperative ECG showed complete right bundle branch block; routine labs were unremarkable. Anesthesia was induced with propofol, fentanyl, remifentanil, and rocuronium, and maintained with sevoflurane, remifentanil, and intermittent rocuronium. Intraoperative hemodynamics and oxygenation remained stable. Surgery lasted 2 h 49 min. After discontinuation of anesthetics, the patient opened his eyes at an end‐tidal sevoflurane concentration of 0.1%–0.2%, received sugammadex, and was extubated. Minutes later, his level of consciousness declined to a Glasgow Coma Scale score of E1V1M1, with stable respiratory status. Naloxone was given without improvement. Body temperature was 37.0 °C. Blood gas analysis showed normal pH and electrolytes, and blood glucose was 110 mg/dL. New right conjugate eye deviation was noted. Head CT and MRI revealed no new infarction or hemorrhage. There were no respiratory or circulatory abnormalities, and he was transferred urgently to the ICU for close observation.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Residual opioid effect considered and excluded — “Considering the possibility of the effect of residual opioids, naloxone was administered, but with no change in the level of consciousness.”  
2. Hypoglycemia considered and excluded — “There were no signs of hypoglycemia (blood sugar 110 mg/dL).”  
3. Electrolyte or acid–base disturbance considered and excluded — “Prompt blood gas analysis was performed, which revealed normal pH and electrolyte levels.”  
4. Intracranial hemorrhage or infarction considered and excluded — “Head computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging scans were performed, but no abnormal findings, such as new brain infarctions or intracranial hemorrhage, were detected.”  
5. Nonconvulsive status epilepticus suspected — “Based on the assumption of an epileptic seizure, 5 mg of diazepam was administered, which resulted in an improvement in the level of consciousness.”
